summary: Agrorikis is a free, mobile-friendly web tool that helps farmers choose their next crop. The farmer pins a field on the map, enters the previous and planned crop, soil traits (texture, pH, organic matter, drainage, slope) and priorities such as saving water or reducing erosion. The tool pulls climate data from NASA POWER, including temperature, rainfall, frost risk and root-zone soil moisture, and compares three rotation strategies: the current plan, a nitrogen-fixing legume option, and an option from a new plant family. Each strategy explains why it was suggested, the evidence behind it, expected benefits, information gaps and risks that local experts should review. It also flags same-family rotations that share pests and diseases, such as whitefly-borne viruses. This matters because climate change and degraded soils make rotation decisions harder, and a wrong choice spreads disease and wastes water. Agrorikis is decision support, not a replacement for the judgment of farmers and agronomists. Next, we plan to add SMAP, GPM IMERG, SRTM and ECOSTRESS data.
details:
What it does and how it works
Agrorikis is a free, lightweight web tool (no installation, works on a phone) that helps a farmer decide what to plant next. The farmer pins a field on an interactive map or with GPS, then enters the previous crop, the planned crop, basic soil traits (texture, pH, organic matter, drainage, slope) and priorities: saving water, improving soil, reducing erosion or extra income. The app instantly queries NASA POWER for the location’s climate: altitude, mean temperature, coldest-month minimum (frost risk), monthly rainfall, dry months and root-zone soil moisture. It then compares three rotation strategies: (A) the farmer’s current plan, (B) the best-fitting nitrogen-fixing legume, and (C) the best option from a different plant family. Every strategy shows why it was suggested, the evidence behind it, benefits, information gaps and risks to review with a local technician. The tool also flags same-family rotations that share pests and diseases, and warns about pests such as whitefly that can carry viruses between families.

Benefits
Farmers get a clear, explainable comparison instead of a guess. Breaking pest and disease cycles, adding legumes for nitrogen, avoiding frost-prone and water-hungry choices, and protecting sloping soils all support healthier soil and lower input costs. The tool also highlights dry months, when fields tend to sit exposed or fallow.

Expected impact
Better rotation decisions can reduce disease pressure and water use, improve soil organic matter and nitrogen, and make smallholder farms more resilient to climate variability. Because it is free, open to anyone with a browser and works anywhere on Earth, it can reach farmers who have no access to agronomic advisory services, while still encouraging them to consult local experts.

Tools and technologies
HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in a single static page, hosted on GitHub Pages. Data: NASA POWER climatology API (temperature, precipitation, frost and root-zone soil wetness, derived from NASA satellite-based models such as MERRA-2 and CERES). Crop climate and altitude ranges are based on FAO EcoCrop-style parameters, adjusted for Andean conditions; plant families and pest-sharing rules come from our agronomy training. We used the AI assistant Claude to help write and refine the code and the presentation.

Creativity
We turned a simple agronomic rule into a decision tool: “never follow a crop with one from the same family” becomes the first filter, then climate fit, soil and farmer priorities rank the alternatives. The three-strategy format, with evidence, gaps and risks for each, keeps the tool honest about uncertainty and keeps the farmer in charge.

Factors we considered
Usability for farmers with little technical experience, low internet requirements, transparency about what the data can and cannot say, and respect for local knowledge. Limitations: climate data comes from a coarse global grid (about 50 km), scores are heuristic and not a calibrated yield model, soil data is entered by the farmer, and market information is not yet included. Our roadmap adds SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG extreme rainfall, SRTM slope, ECOSTRESS heat stress and Landsat/Sentinel-2 vegetation indices.
